clue.text: Removed someone from house, a horror of mine

parts.note: fired means removed from a job
an MP is a Member of Parliament, someone who sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: An eviction from a home is called a horror of mine, as if a landlord were speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the House of Commons, not a dwelling: its members are MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the explosive methane gas found in coal mines, a miner's great dread.

clue.text: Brother officer was head of state

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar, a religious brother
NCO is short for non-commissioned officer, such as a sergeant

explanation.surface: A soldier from a religious order once ran the country.
explanation.definitionFit: General Franco was Spain's dictator and head of state from 1939 to 1975.

clue.text: Look, that's not neat spirit, wise guy

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
a mage is a magus, a wise man

explanation.surface: Someone at a bar is told their spirit should not be drunk straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not neat' seems to be about a drink served without water; it belongs to the definition, describing an untidy search.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search by turning things over untidily, a look that leaves a mess.

clue.text: Beautifully-crafted period toys housed here

indicators.note: something crafted is put together with skill, so these letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A display of fine antique toys is kept in a storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beautifully-crafted' rearranges PERIOD TOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A depository is a storehouse, a place where goods are kept safely.

clue.text: Into computer, I processed film

indicators.note: processed data is changed by working on it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone feeds footage into a computer for editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges INTO COMPUTER I.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion picture is a cinema film, a sequence of moving images.

clue.text: Policeman has to go over to arrest duke

indicators.note: something that arrests another holds it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to recap is to go over the main points again

explanation.surface: An officer must review the arrest of an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is the British nickname for a member of the Royal Military Police.

clue.text: Asteroid that's landed in very centre of London?

definitions.meaning: A near-Earth minor planet, named after the Greek god of love

definitions.text: that's landed in very centre of London?
definitions.meaning: the winged statue at Piccadilly Circus, a London landmark, is popularly called by the love god's name

explanation.surface: Something from space has come down right in the middle of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue in Piccadilly Circus, the junction many regard as London's centre, is popularly known as Eros, so the god has 'landed' there.
explanation.definitionFit: The asteroid and the Piccadilly statue both bear the name of the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Injured, and worse? Pay no attention arch

parts.note: cut means wounded or injured
dead is worse than injured

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a victim is merely hurt or worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to snub them, ignoring them completely.

clue.text: Describes fish beneath side of boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
rays are flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone sees fish swimming under the side of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or describe in words or pictures.

clue.text: End of the road?

definitions.meaning: a goal, an end in view
the A1(M) is a British motorway, which written as A1M looks like these three letters

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether this is where the road runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1(M) is a motorway in Britain; read with the digit 1 as letter I it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is the end one strives for, a purpose or goal.

clue.text: Prayer gives us a lift

definitions.meaning: the Lord's Prayer, named from its Latin opening words Our Father
a continuous lift of open cars that never stops, once common in British office buildings

explanation.surface: Saying one's prayers gives a spiritual boost.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternoster is both the Lord's Prayer and a type of continuously moving elevator.

clue.text: Confirmation perhaps of authority to go on speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the words are said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a right of passage is the entitlement to go on through a place

explanation.surface: A permit to continue a speech is granted by an official.
explanation.walkthrough: Confirmation, the church ceremony, is an example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony marking a transition in life, such as confirmation, is an example of this ritual.

clue.text: House that's big enough for a talk?

definitions.text: House that's big enough for a talk?

parts.words: House that's big enough for a talk?
parts.note: read as a phrase meaning 'value of a chat', it names a famous stately home in Derbyshire

explanation.surface: Someone asks which mansion would be spacious enough to hold a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Chatsworth House is a great stately home in Derbyshire, England; split as CHAT'S WORTH it means what a talk is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth is the Duke of Devonshire's famous stately home in Derbyshire.

clue.text: Heartless composer makes a tragic figure

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: Franz Lehar wrote the operetta The Merry Widow

explanation.surface: An unfeeling musician turns into someone out of a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the central H of LEHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Pig-headed, disposing of property without lawyer?

definitions.meaning: stubbornly insisting on one's own way
having written one's own will, leaving one's estate without a solicitor's help

explanation.surface: A stubborn person insists on making their own will without legal help.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-willed means obstinate and determined to have one's own way.

clue.text: Trail heard leading to London, not taken seriously

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves
up is the direction of travel to London, traditionally going up to town

explanation.surface: A trail one hears about runs towards the capital, but nobody believes it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage one goes 'up' to London from anywhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent up means mocked or satirised, treated as a joke rather than seriously.

clue.text: When surgeon's finished, always possible to look freely round now

definitions.text: possible to look freely round now

parts.note: the end of an operation, OP END
ay is an old poetic word for always, also spelt aye

explanation.surface: After surgery the patient may always walk about and look around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the occasion: an open day is a day when the public is free to look round a school or institution.
explanation.definitionFit: On an open day visitors may tour a place that is normally closed to them.

clue.text: Pay better, though one is on the bottle

parts.note: screw is old British slang for wages
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Higher wages are demanded, though one worker is a drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the bottle' suggests a drinker, but the screwcap literally sits on the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwcap is a threaded lid fitted on the neck of a bottle.

clue.text: In academic stream, reliable type not finishing material

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

indicators.note: a word that is not finishing stops short of its end, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, solid sort of person

explanation.surface: A dependable person in a university river fails to get to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the K of BRICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: Unease people of peninsula expressed The Tim

indicators.note: expressed means put into spoken words, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the Malays are the people of the Malay Peninsula

explanation.surface: Residents of a peninsula voice their disquiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tim' after 'expressed' is a stray OCR fragment and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a vague feeling of unease or discomfort.

clue.text: Stink raised about diver

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell
up means raised

explanation.surface: A bad smell rises around a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NIFF UP round to give the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: She's artless and sincere in being well brought up

definitions.text: She's artless and sincere in being well brought up

parts.words: She's artless and sincere in being well brought up
parts.note: a portrait of a naive, innocent young woman, as in the stock theatrical role

explanation.surface: A girl is described as naive and genuine because of her good upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: Right of pair to cross barrier perhaps

indicators.note: one piece crosses the other, set inside it

parts.note: a rope is one kind of barrier

explanation.surface: Two people try to get over a fence the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' puts ROPE inside PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means right, correct or appropriate.

clue.text: Fish, not quite glossily healthy, sent back

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means it falls one letter short at the end

parts.note: sleek describes a smooth glossy coat in good condition

explanation.surface: A fish not looking its best is returned to the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims SLEEK to SLEE and 'sent back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Nursing leg shot by him?

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tends an injured leg after a gunfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges NURSING LEG; the whole clue also describes the victim of a gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger is a gunfighter, especially of the Wild West.

clue.text: Baby son shows intelligence

parts.note: new means newly born, as a baby is

explanation.surface: A newborn boy displays early cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' means information, not cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of information or reports.

clue.text: Imaginary barrier? Real one's great

definitions.meaning: an information barrier within a firm, preventing confidential matters passing between departments
the actual one is the Great Wall of China

explanation.surface: A wall that exists only in the mind is contrasted with a real and impressive one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese wall is a notional barrier in a financial firm; the real one is the Great Wall.

clue.text: Tip some winks?

definitions.meaning: in horse racing, a tipster's best bet of the day
forty winks means a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone advises taking a short rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is both a racing tip and a short sleep.

clue.text: This is polite to add finally to requests

definitions.text: This is polite to add finally to requests

parts.note: pleas are requests

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word polite

explanation.surface: A courteous word should be tacked on to the end of any request.
explanation.definitionFit: Please is the polite word added when making a request.

clue.text: Mortarboard, especially?

parts.note: a builder's board for mortar suggests equipment, but here it is the academic cap worn on graduation

explanation.surface: A builder's mortarboard is held up as a prime example of kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortarboard, the square academic cap, is an item worn on the head.
